purpose: Run the released configuration unchanged on a second revision of this repository, to check two things the release alone cannot show: that the pipeline reproduces end to end on a corpus it has never seen, and that a full-size artifact -- not a small smoke checkpoint -- installs through the operator CLI and is served by the core.

corpusReverification.method: git archive <revision> | tar -x -C <dir>, then build_manifest over that tree
corpusReverification.note: The first run whose corpus is reproducible from a commit with no uncommitted-tree caveat: the revision was read beside the corpus, it carries no -dirty suffix, and the digest recomputed from that revision's own text is the digest the report records. The recomputation ran before the training finished, so the match is a prediction that held rather than a check fitted to the answer.

previousVerificationRun.note: Kept alongside this one because it was measured on a tree that carried uncommitted changes, and its corpus included this project's own build products. Both facts are recorded there; this run is the one without them.

What carried over is the configuration and the gate, not the number.

storeUpdateAndRollback.method: services/core/scripts/klyvaron.mjs install <dir> [--replace] --data-dir <dir>, with two artifacts of the same id and different weights: aetheris-lite-lm@0.1.0-verify (2840150fa754b126...) and aetheris-lite-lm@0.1.1-verify (165e150f6e290fe3...)

steps.step: 1. a device holding the earlier verification artifact (0.1.0-verify, sha 2840150f...)
2. the newer artifact arrives (0.1.1-verify, sha 165e150f...): refused without an explicit replace
3. an explicit replace: verify, budget, copy, re-verify, re-record -- the weights digest changes
4. verify the library: the bytes on disk match the new manifest
5. rollback: the device reinstalls the artifact it was running, and the digest returns to 2840150f...
6. a corrupted copy of the newer artifact: refused even with --replace
7. the library is untouched by the refusal: still 0.1.0-verify, still verifiable

storeUpdateAndRollback.finding: This is where a real defect surfaced. Replacing one version with another used to merge the new files into the existing directory, leaving the previous version's 1.4 MB weights behind with no manifest referring to them -- invisible to verify(), never reclaimed, and counted twice by the install report (which measured the source directory rather than what the device ended up holding). After the rollback the library held 2,898,235 bytes for one artifact id. services/core/src/klyvaron/store.mjs now clears the artifact's own directory when replacing, charges the budget only the growth, and reports the measured result; klyvaron-store.test.mjs covers the version-to-version replace and fails against the old code. With the fix the same rollback leaves 1,451,373 bytes.

servingReleased.note: Recorded after the promotion, with the export the model card describes: aetheris-lite-lm@0.1.1 with no qualifier. The install above was captured with a 0.1.1-verify manifest -- the same weights, the same file digest, a version string 14 bytes shorter. That is the whole difference between the two captures, and this pair is what makes it checkable.

note: Committed record of a measured run. Absolute paths from the machine that produced it are canonicalised; every measured value is unchanged. The weights and this report's own JSON are not committed: artifacts stay out of Git by policy and are referenced by digest. This run's artifact is the released aetheris-lite-lm@0.1.1 (see docs/model-cards/); the install and serve evidence below was captured before the version was promoted and therefore names the artifact as aetheris-lite-lm@0.1.1-verify -- the same weights and the same file digest, a different version string in the manifest.
